note: Broad-vs-deep capacity (tier-slot mechanic). skillsKnownByLevel = max DISTINCT chosen abilities a character may hold at each level — the breadth cap. Level 1 = 2 (Erik ratified 2026-07-06: 'generic RPG quantity per level guide, level 1 = 2'). At the cap, skill points may still RANK UP owned abilities (depth) — that IS the broad-vs-deep tradeoff. Tier access is separately gated by each ability's levelReq. Generic linear default (level + 1); tunable.
tierPriceNote: SNG-260 §D / SNG-261 §A — what a craft is WORTH, by its levelReq tier. Erik: 'a Tier-II costs 2, a Tier-III costs 3. Power costs more.' Composes MULTIPLICATIVELY with the distance term (domain ring penalty, or the cross-class multiplier when domains are unset), so a far Tier-III is genuinely dear and a near Tier-I stays 1. The catalog holds 28 abilities at levelReq 4 and 26 at levelReq 5, so the ladder must reach T-V (SNG-261 §A); this default is LINEAR — whether T-IV/V accelerate (4/6 rather than 4/5) is Erik's dial. Earned growth (practice, braids, discoveries) never comes through this table.
rule: LEARN a new ability only while distinct-ability count < skillsKnownByLevel[level]. At the cap, points go to depth (rank-ups). Emergence combos/branches (SNG-010) and crit-discoveries do NOT count against the cap — earned techniques are free growth, not chosen breadth.

crossClass.ratified: Erik 2026-07-06 — soft class cap: secondary-class abilities cost double, no hard rank ceiling
crossClass.homeClass: the character's origin power system (harmonic|radiant|valley_craft); precursor is learned-only
crossClass.note: Learning OR ranking an ability whose powerSystem is NOT the character's home class costs 2x skill points. No hard rank-2 ceiling — you CAN master a secondary class, it just costs. Preserves specialist-vs-generalist tension via price, not a wall. Stacks with the existing cross-training +1 levelReq. Precursor point-spend (after unlock) also pays the multiplier if precursor isn't home.
